'''''Copernicia prunifera''''' or the '''carnaúba palm''' or '''carnaubeira palm''' ({{IPA|pt|kaʁnaˈubɐ}}) is a [[species]] of [[palm tree]] native to northeastern [[Brazil]] (mainly the states of Ceará, Piauí, Maranhão, Rio Grande do Norte and Bahia). Known by many as 'tree of life' because of its many uses, the Carnaúba is also the symbol tree of [[Ceará]]. The initiative to use it as a symbol vies to promote its conservation and sustainable use.<ref>FREITAS, Vicente. ''BELA CRUZ — biografia do município''. [[Joinville]]: [[Clube de Autores]], 2013, pp. 144-53. {{ISBN|978-85-916141-0-3}}</ref>

==Plant description==
''Copernica prunifera'' can grow up to 20 m height with an average 25 cm diameter trunk, circular tree crown, with fan-leaves measuring 1.5 m, bisexual flowers and small black round fruits (2.5 cm). The palm can live up to 200 years.<ref name=Duke>{{cite book|last1=Duke|first1=James A.|last2=duCellier|first2=Judith L.|title=CRC handbook of alternative cash crops|date=1993|publisher=CRC Press|location=Boca Raton|isbn=978-0-8493-3620-1|page=536|edition=3rd}}</ref>
Although it withstands drought well, it has a high water requirement for growth. A slightly saline composition in the soil produces the best trees. Carnaubas are social palm trees, they are found in Carnaubais (assembly/group of Carnaubas) in flood zones or near rivers. 
Taxonomically, this tree belongs to the subfamily Coryphoideae, tribe Corypheae, subtribe Livistoninae.

==Biodiversity==

The Carnauba palm tree is an endemic species to the [[Caatinga]], an exclusive Brazilian biome, comprising a total area of 826,411 km². The latter is present in eight of the nine Northeastern states: Piauí, Ceará, Rio Grande do Norte, Paraíba, Pernambuco, Alagoas, Sergipe, Bahia,
and it is also present in a northern strip of Minas Gerais. Caatinga covers approximately 10% of the national territory and 70% of the
Northeast region, and borders with three other biomes in the country, the [[Amazon rainforest]], the [[Atlantic Forest]], and [[Cerrado]] savanna. A semiarid climate prevails in the Caatinga, with approximately 800 mm of poorly distributed rainfall per year, resulting in long periods of drought.
The carnauba palm tree, is an easily adaptable species and, thus, is spread over large territories, greatly impacting the locations.
Besides economic and cultural impacts, it has a remarkable ecological influence of this northeastern palm on the environments.
The fact that the carnauba palm tree is a species that grows along rivers and streams in general, helps to prevent siltation in the
water bodies and to control soil erosion in the areas where it is located.
The fruits of the carnauba palm tree serve as food for animals such as bats, pigs, wild hogs and some Psittacidae (parrots and parakeets),
one of the best assisting factors in spreading the seeds of this species. Bees also consume nectar and pollen from its flowers to make
honey, helping to pollinate this species. Nevertheless, the relationship between the carnauba palm tree and animals is not limited to feeding, but is also related to aiding migration processes and balancing the ecosystem. Birds, for example, often use this palm tree to nest and rest when flocking.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.acaatinga.org.br/wp-content/uploads/carnauba_production_chain_-_good_practices_manual.pdf |last=Associacao Caatinga |first=BMU-IKI/GIZ |date=2019 |title=Good Practices Manual for the Carnauba supply chain |access-date=2019-12-05 |archive-date=2019-12-05 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191205165403/https://www.acaatinga.org.br/wp-content/uploads/carnauba_production_chain_-_good_practices_manual.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Uses==
It is the source of [[carnauba wax]], which is harvested as a natural coating from the surface of the leaves of the tree. The fruit and pith are eaten, the leaves are variously utilized and the wood is a construction material.

===Edible parts===
Carnauba produces several materials that have versatile applications. Its fruits can be used as feed to cattle, donkeys, goats and pigs or can also be used to produce jelly for human consumption. The pulp is extracted and dried to produce carnauba flour, largely consumed by natives.
Cooking oil can be extracted from the seeds, which are also edible. When roasted, fruits are ground and brewed to make a drink that can be used as a substitute for coffee.<ref name=Duke /><ref name=Cerratinga>{{cite web|title=Carnaúba|url=http://www.cerratinga.org.br/carnauba/|website=Cerratinga, Produção Sustentável e Consumo Consciente|publisher=Instituto Sociedade, População e Natureza|access-date=3 November 2015}}</ref><ref name=Nogueira>{{cite web|last1=Nogueira|first1=Djalma H.|title=Qualidade e potencial de utilização de frutos de genótipo de carnaubeira (''Copernicia prunifera'') oriundos do estado do Ceará|url=http://www.alice.cnptia.embrapa.br/alice/bitstream/doc/697462/1/OT09016.pdf|publisher=UFPB|access-date=3 November 2015}}</ref>

===Carnauba wax===
{{main|Carnauba wax}}
The most important product of the Carnauba tree is the wax extracted from its leaves.<ref name=Nogueira/> It can be used in floor, leather, furniture, car and shoe polish, and is used in the manufacture of carbon paper, candles, chalk, matches, soap and woodwork stains.<ref name=Duke /><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Steinle|first1=J. Vernon|title=Carnauba Wax: An expedition to Its Source|journal=Industrial & Engineering Chemistry|date=September 1936|volume=28|issue=9|pages=1004–1008|doi=10.1021/ie50321a003}}<!--|accessdate=3 November 2015--></ref>
It consists of myricyl cerotate and small quantities of cerotic acid and myricyl alcohol.<ref name=Duke />

After harvesting, the leaves are left upon the field to dry under the sun. The thin layer of wax coating plant material disintegrates into a powder, which is then separated through beating and whisking the dried leaves. The powder is concentrated in a mortar, to be mixed with water and melted to produce liquid wax. After drying it is concentrated into chunks and sold.<ref name=Cerratinga/><ref name=video1>{{cite web|last1=Oliveira|first1=Fabélia|title=Produção da Carnaúba no Rio Grande do Norte|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=f1oljf0V0jI|access-date=3 November 2015}}</ref>

===Leaf fibers===
The leaf fibers are a byproduct of the wax production, known as "bagana".  The biomass can be used as compost, soil coverage to maintain humidity, or compressed into biofuel briquettes with a high energy content for power generation. The leaf fibers, or "palha", are also woven in the manufacture of objects such as hats, baskets, bags and many other domestic products (Steinle and Johnson, 1935; Duke and duCellier). These handicraft products are beloved by tourists and represent an important source of income to the local population. The wax palm leaves can also be used in rustic roof making.

===Wood===
Due to the natural resistance against the most common wood pests, such as termites, Carnauba Wood is a valued local construction material. Although it is mainly used by people with low income, its function in beach tents – not only as central pillar/column/post, but also as the leaf roof – is very common.

The {{ill|Mercado de Carne de Aquiraz|pt}}, in Ceará, is one notable example of Carnauba Wood effectiveness as a versatile construction material.<ref name=HPIP>{{cite web|title=Mercado da Carne|url=https://hpip.org/pt/Heritage/Details/957|website=Património de Influência Portuguesa|publisher=Fundação Calouste Gulbenkian|access-date=9 March 2023}}</ref><ref name=IPATRIMONIO>{{cite web|title=Aquiraz – Mercado de Carne e Lojas Adjacentes|url=http://www.ipatrimonio.org/aquiraz-mercado-de-carne-e-lojas-adjacentes/#!/map=38329&loc=-3.901716000000003,-38.38999599999999,17|publisher=Ipatrimônio|access-date=9 March 2023}}</ref> While the roof of the building is supported by [[trusses]] and beams consisting of the whole Carnauba trunk, the ceramic [[roof tiles]] are carefully fitted atop rafters made from the same wood, cut in four equal sections.

==Cultivation==
It withstands drought well. A slightly saline composition in the soil produces the best trees.

==Harvest==
[[File:Harvest tool.jpeg|thumb|Figure 1: Carnaúba harvest tool.<ref>{{Cite web|title = COLHEITA DE CARNAÚBA|url = http://www.consciencia.org/colheita-de-carnauba|website = www.consciencia.org|access-date = 2015-11-27|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20151208102054/http://www.consciencia.org/colheita-de-carnauba|archive-date = 2015-12-08|url-status = dead}}</ref>]] 
To produce wax, harvesting operations have to be employed during the dry season to assure complete drying of the leaves. The harvest is normally done from August to December. However, during periods of longer winters, the harvest may be delayed.<ref name=video1/> 
A Carnuaba palm tree can produce up to 60 leaves per plant, especially after a very intense rainy season.<ref name=alvescoelho>{{cite web|last1=Alves|first1=Maria O.|last2=Coelho|first2=Jackson D.|title=Extrativismo da Carnaúba: O Desafio de Estimar os Resultados Econômicos|url=http://www.sober.org.br/palestra/9/756.pdf|publisher=Sociedade Brasileira de Economia e Administração (SOBER)|access-date=3 November 2015}}</ref> 
Harvested with a long pole ending in a hooked blade (Figure 1), the top leaves are removed for superior wax content. To maintain sustainable production of Carnauba, cuttings are performed three times a year, in 80 day intervals from each tree.<ref name=Duke /><ref name=video1/>
Production of Carnauba-derived materials dropped in the beginning of the 1970s, especially due to the invention of synthetic and [[petroleum product]]s.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Johnson|first1=Dennis, V.|last2=Nair|first2=P. K. R.|title=Perennial crop-based agroforestry systems in Northeast Brazil|journal=Agroforestry Systems|date=1985|volume=2|issue=4|pages=281–292|doi=10.1007/BF00147039|s2cid=24232541}}</ref> Since then, the production has increased in the beginning of the 2000s and reached around 20,000 tons of powder and around 2,500 tons of wax, which has been sustained since then.<ref name=sidra>{{cite web|url=http://www.sidra.ibge.gov.br/bda/extveg/default.asp?z=t&o=18&i=P|title=Brasil|website=Sistema IBGE de Recuperação Automática - SIDRA|language=pt|access-date=3 November 2015}}</ref>

==Economy==
Carnauba economical activity includes the extraction and utilization of [[Leaf|leaves]], [[Plant stem|stem]], [[TAL effector|tale]] and [[Fiber|fibre]], [[fruit]]s and [[root]]s. These materials are all manufactured into crafted and industrialized products.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Carvalho|first1=José N. F.|last2=Gomes|first2=Jaíra M. A.|title=Contribuição de Extrativismo da Carnaúba para Mitigação da Pobreza no Nordeste|url=http://www.ecoeco.org.br/conteudo/publicacoes/encontros/vii_en/mesa5/trabalhos/contribuicao_do_extrativismo_da_carnauba.pdf|website=Enconomia Ecológica|publisher=VII Encontro da Sociedade Brasileira de Economia Ecológica - 2007|access-date=3 November 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304030313/http://www.ecoeco.org.br/conteudo/publicacoes/encontros/vii_en/mesa5/trabalhos/contribuicao_do_extrativismo_da_carnauba.pdf|archive-date=4 March 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>
However, the powder used in wax production is the most profitable part of the plant due to great market interest.<ref name="alvescoelho"/>
The production of Carnauba is mainly found in Northeastern [[Brazil]], especially in the [[Rio Grande do Norte]] state (5%), [[Ceará]] state (35%) and in [[Piauí]] state (45%). Brazil is the only exporting country, and the main importers are [[Japan]], [[United States]] and also [[Europe]].<ref name=sidra /><ref>{{cite web|title=Cera de carnaúba é um dos principais produtos de exportação do Piauí|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BwNut7cX4xU |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211213/BwNut7cX4xU |archive-date=2021-12-13 |url-status=live|publisher=Cidade Verde|access-date=2 November 2015}}{{cbignore}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Conjuntura Mensal - Março 2013|url=http://www.conab.gov.br/OlalaCMS/uploads/arquivos/13_04_23_17_23_27_carnauba__(po_e_cera).pdf|website=Companhia Nacional do Abastecimento (CONAB)|access-date=2 November 2015}}</ref>
